name: US dollar
summary: Dollar index near 103.2 on 13 Nov, a 52-week high, up 3.5% over three months; inside Normal lines
state: The DXY dollar index was near 103.2 early on 13 Nov, its highest in a year, up 3.5% over three months and 1.5% on the week (Yahoo Finance). That is inside the 5% three-month Watch line and the 90–108 range. SOFR was 1bp below the Fed's reserve rate on 10 Nov, showing no dollar funding strain (FRED).
for_you: A firmer dollar makes dollar-priced goods such as fuel slightly dearer in pounds and euros, and raises costs for countries with dollar debts.
rubric_hit: DXY 3m move 3.5% below the 5% Watch line; level 103.2 inside 90–108
why: The dollar is the world's funding currency; violent moves squeeze emerging markets and anyone with dollar debts.
drivers: Fed vs other central banks, safe-haven demand, trade policy, reserve diversification.

rubric.alert: DXY moved > 8% in 3 months, or dollar funding stress (Fed swap lines drawn materially).
rubric.watch: DXY moved 5–8% in 3 months, or outside 90–108.
rubric.normal: DXY moved < 5% over 3 months and is between 90 and 108.
